intro: Hi again! This lesson builds your first useful word bank: everyday things and people, numbers from 1 to 20, and simple colours and adjectives. Warm-up: name one thing you can see near you right now — in English, if you can!
teachingNotes: Teach words in small groups with an Indonesian gloss.
Numbers 13–19 end in -teen; learners confuse thirteen/thirty, fifteen/fifty — stress -TEEN.
Adjectives come BEFORE nouns in English (a red car = mobil merah); Indonesian puts them after.
Accept British or American spellings (colour/color, grey/gray).

keyPoints.title: Everyday nouns
keyPoints.explanation: People: mother, father, friend, teacher. Places: house, school, office, market. Things: phone, book, table, water.

examples.en: a friend, a teacher, a house
a phone, a book, a table

keyPoints.title: Numbers 1–20
keyPoints.explanation: one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten, eleven, twelve, then thirteen to nineteen with -teen, and twenty.

keyPoints.title: Colours and adjectives go before the noun
keyPoints.explanation: Colours: red, blue, green, yellow, black, white. Adjectives: big, small, new, old, hot, cold. Say 'a red car', not 'a car red'.

guidedPractice.hint: The colour comes first in English.

id.intro: Hai lagi! Pelajaran ini membangun kosakata pertamamu yang berguna: benda dan orang sehari-hari, angka 1 sampai 20, serta warna dan kata sifat sederhana. Pemanasan: sebutkan satu benda yang bisa kamu lihat di dekatmu sekarang — dalam bahasa Inggris, kalau bisa!
